stem: In a government school in Pune, a measles vaccination camp is held before the monsoon. Meera's grandmother asks why healthy children are being vaccinated. Which statement best explains how vaccination reduces serious infections and their spread?

options.text: Vaccines are medicines taken after someone falls sick, so they cure measles and stop it spreading.
Vaccines prepare the immune system before exposure, so vaccinated children are less likely to become seriously ill and less likely to pass the infection to others.
The first exposure to measles produces the stronger immune response, so vaccination is only useful after a child has already had measles once.
Children in the same class share the same immunity, so vaccinating a few children protects the whole class equally.

teacher.key_rationale: Vaccination builds immune protection before or around exposure, reducing serious illness and onward transmission; only option B states this. A reverses vaccine purpose (cure after sickness), C reverses primary/secondary response strength, D captures the surface feature that classmates share immunity equally.
